items.question: Under Council Directive 93/13/EEC, when is a contract term regarded as unfair, and when is a term treated as not individually negotiated?
items.reference_answer: A term that has not been individually negotiated is unfair if, contrary to good faith, it causes a significant imbalance in the parties' rights and obligations under the contract, to the detriment of the consumer. A term is always regarded as not individually negotiated where it was drafted in advance and the consumer has not been able to influence its substance, particularly in a pre-formulated standard contract.
